title: introduce-gradual-schema-flag-and-streaming-fallback-shim
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds opt-in schema header and server-side compatibility shim with streaming fallback. Deprecation warnings for legacy schema behavior. No user-visible breaking changes if opt-in not used.
description:
Motivation: We need a low-friction path to introduce a schema v3 (structured output / tool-calling harmonization) while preserving existing OpenAI-compatible clients and streaming semantics. This PR adds a conservative, opt-in compatibility flag and a server-side shim that gracefully falls back streaming to a polling pathway when a client/server schema mismatch prevents stable event streaming.

Summary of changes (single-line summary): introduce X-Redwood-Schema header, 'Prefer: schema=v3-beta' opt-in, server shim that maps v2->v1 fields for compatibility, streaming handshake fallback, updates to function-call and structured-output mapping in the openai-compat layer, tests and docs.

Checklist: - [x] Add opt-in request header parsing (X-Redwood-Schema / Prefer) - [x] Implement server-side mapping shim (turns/messages, json_schema/structured_output) - [x] Streaming handshake: detect schema-negotiation mismatch and emit fallback control event - [x] Add telemetry events for fallback occurrences - [x] Unit/integration tests across Go runtime + TS SDK mapping - [x] Docs: migration notes + deprecation timeline - [x] E2E compatibility tests with legacy clients

Commits (high-level): 1) Add header parsing and schema negotiation in compat handler 2) Implement v3->v2 field mapping shim and canonicalizer 3) Streaming handshake: add 'schema-compatible' probe, streaming-fallback route and polling link 4) Function-calling adapter: accept both function_call and call_instruction shapes, normalize to runtime shape 5) Structured-output adapter: map json_schema -> structured_output and vice versa, sanitize extra_properties 6) Tests + fixtures 7) Docs and changelog

Files/areas touched (high-level): - server/compat/negotiation.go (new) - server/compat/shims.go (new) - server/compat/streaming_fallback.go (new) - runtime/handler.go (compat hooks) - openai-compat/adapter.ts (mapping helpers) - sdk/ts/tests/compat_streaming.test.ts - docs/migrations/schema-v3-beta.md - ci/workflows/compat-tests.yml

Small illustrative snippet (compat negotiation pseudocode):

// on request
// 1) parse headers: X-Redwood-Schema OR Prefer: schema=v3-beta
// 2) if request asks for v3 semantics but server not yet capable -> attempt shim
// 3) if streaming handshake fails due to structural mismatch -> return 204 + Link: <polling>/status and emit telemetry

Review conversation (abridged, in-thread):
- Arjun: "Can we guarantee no change for existing clients when no header is provided? Add explicit opt-in tests."
- Maya: "Yes — default behaviour is unchanged. Added integration tests that exercise blank header and Prefer header negative case (tests/compat_default_blank_header)."
- Lena: "Streaming fallback is clever but we need to measure latency tax. Please add a metric: streaming.compat.fallback.latency distribution."
- Maya: "Added telemetry event streaming.compat.fallback.{count,lat_p50,p95} and a dashboard note in docs."
- Diego: "Function calling adapters must preserve original user-visible signatures for OpenAI-compat clients. Validate no loss of argument typing."
- Maya: "Adapter preserves argument blob; when converting between JSON-string and object we include original raw_arguments on the runtime context for audits."

CI notes: initial run showed an e2e flake in the TS SDK streaming harness (race in event buffer). I fixed by adding a short retry in the harness and hardened the mock server to assert schema-negotiation header ordering. Final run: all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e, lint, benchmarks).

Design/behavior details: - Header surface: X-Redwood-Schema: v1 | v2 | v3-beta (canonical). We also honor Prefer: schema=v3-beta for HTTP clients. Absent header = v2 compatibility. - Opt-in semantics: v3-beta enables stricter structured output enforcement, canonical variable names for tool-calling, and explicit schema-driven streaming events (delta types). Servers accept v3-beta only when runtime feature-flag enabled; otherwise respond with 412 + guidance or silently shim (configurable per-deployment). - Shim behavior: When a v3-beta request arrives at a runtime not fully v3-capable but our compat layer can do a safe mapping, we apply the shim to translate request/response shapes. For streaming: we attempt the normal streaming handshake; if an early mismatch is detected (response frames not parseable by client schema), we abort server-sent events stream and emit a small control event to the client with "streaming_fallback": true and a Link header to a compensating polling endpoint (/compat/poll/<id>). The client receives a 204 No Content body for the stream and can continue by polling; meanwhile we schedule the full response to be available at the polling route. - Telemetry: new events streaming.compat.fallback.count, streaming.compat.fallback.latency_p50, streaming.compat.fallback.latency_p95, compat.schema.negotiation.failure. - Deprecation timeline: v1 behaviour (implicit 'messages' only) is now marked deprecated in favor of v2 canonical names. We will send X-Schema-Deprecation: v1; will not break existing clients for 12 months. Docs include migration recipe and code samples.

Backward compatibility notes: - No changes for clients that do not opt into v3-beta headers. - For opt-in clients, the shim aims to preserve semantics; however, because some v3 features (schema-validated streaming frames) are newer, we provide the fallback so production users don't observe silent truncation.

Testing: added 18 new unit tests and 5 e2e scenarios exercising streaming fallback with mismatched shapes, function_call shapes, and structured-output edge cases. Load bench: added a micro-bench that simulates 1000 small streaming requests; fallback path measured additional median latency of ~18ms for negotiated fallbacks (telemetry recorded in benchmark harness).

Docs: docs/migrations/schema-v3-beta.md includes recommended headers, server responses to expect, and sample code in Python and TS for doing graceful client-side fallback handling.

Follow-ups (future work captured in ENG-2160): - Server can advertise supported schema versions in OPTIONS /status endpoint - Automated rollout gating: only enable shim for a percentage of users initially - SDK helpers: client-side automatics to retry as polling when receiving a fallback control event - Consider making fallback link a resumable websocket handle for lower-latency recovery

Merge notes: Squashed and merged to main after reviewer approvals. No prod config flip was performed in this PR; deployment requires runtime feature-flag enablement per-cluster.

If you want to test locally: see docs/migrations/schema-v3-beta.md and run `make compat-test` in the openai-compat package.

References: Linear ENG-2147 (schema v3 rollout), ENG-2160 (streaming compatibility plan).
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: opt-in, telemetry-first, with a clear fallback path to preserve production stability for streaming and tool-calling clients.
